data: Which line is the most consistently accurate (showing the least variation in accuracy) as dimensionality increases?

The question asks which line shows the least variation in accuracy as dimensionality increases. From the analysis of the figure:

1. The blue line represents the "Proposed" method.
2. The green line represents the "GloVe" method.
3. The red line represents the "NA" method.

Looking at the variations in each line:
- The "Proposed" line remains relatively flat with minimal fluctuations across all dimensions.
- The "GloVe" line shows more noticeable fluctuations, especially after approximately 400 dimensions.
- The "NA" line remains constant at the lowest value throughout the range.

Based on this observation, the "Proposed" line appears to have the least variation in accuracy as dimensionality increases.
